examples.question_text:
A particle moves along a straight line with displacement $x(t)=2t^3-5t^2+4t+6$ metres, where $t\ge0$ is measured in seconds. Right is positive.
(a) Write its initial velocity in derivative notation.
(b) Find its velocity function.
(c) Find its initial velocity and its velocity after $2$ seconds, interpreting their signs.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Initial velocity is $x'(0)$.

(b) $\begin{aligned}v(t)&=\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=6t^2-10t+4\end{aligned}$

(c) $\begin{aligned}v(0)&=6(0)^2-10(0)+4\\&=4\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}v(2)&=6(2)^2-10(2)+4\\&=8\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

Both velocities are positive, so the particle is moving right at both times.

examples.question_text: A particle has displacement $x(t)=t^3-9t^2+15t+4$ metres for $t\ge0$, with $t$ in seconds. Find every time when it is at rest and its displacement at each time.
examples.solution_text:
$v(t)=3t^2-18t+15$.

At rest, $v(t)=0$.

$\begin{aligned}3t^2-18t+15&=0\\3(t-1)(t-5)&=0\end{aligned}$

The particle is at rest at $t=1\text{ s}$ and $t=5\text{ s}$.

$\begin{aligned}x(1)&=1^3-9(1)^2+15(1)+4\\&=11\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}x(5)&=5^3-9(5)^2+15(5)+4\\&=-21\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A particle moves with displacement $x(t)=t^2-9t+18$ metres for $t\ge0$, where $t$ is in seconds. Right is positive. Find the times when it passes through the origin and its velocity at each time.
examples.solution_text:
At the origin, $x(t)=0$.

$\begin{aligned}t^2-9t+18&=0\\(t-3)(t-6)&=0\end{aligned}$

The particle passes through the origin at $t=3\text{ s}$ and $t=6\text{ s}$.

$v(t)=2t-9$.

$\begin{aligned}v(3)&=2(3)-9\\&=-3\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}v(6)&=2(6)-9\\&=3\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

It moves left at the first passage and right at the second.

examples.question_text: A particle has displacement $x(t)=t^2-8t+12$ metres for $t\ge0$, where $t$ is in seconds. Find its velocity the first time its displacement is $5\text{ m}$.
examples.solution_text:
Set $x(t)=5$.

$\begin{aligned}t^2-8t+12&=5\\t^2-8t+7&=0\\(t-1)(t-7)&=0\end{aligned}$

The first time is $t=1\text{ s}$.

$v(t)=2t-8$.

$\begin{aligned}v(1)&=2(1)-8\\&=-6\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Two particles move along the same straight line. Their displacements are $x_A(t)=t^2+4t$ and $x_B(t)=t^3-2t^2-5t+7$ metres for $t\ge0$, with $t$ in seconds. Find when they have the same velocity.
examples.solution_text:
$v_A(t)=2t+4$ and $v_B(t)=3t^2-4t-5$.

Set $v_A(t)=v_B(t)$.

$\begin{aligned}2t+4&=3t^2-4t-5\\3t^2-6t-9&=0\\3(t-3)(t+1)&=0\end{aligned}$

The roots are $t=3$ and $t=-1$. Since $t\ge0$, they have the same velocity at $t=3\text{ s}$.

examples.question_text: A particle moves along a straight line with displacement $x(t)=t^3-12t^2+36t+5$ metres for $t\ge0$, where $t$ is in seconds. Right is positive. Find the interval during which it moves left.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}v(t)&=3t^2-24t+36\\&=3(t-2)(t-6)\end{aligned}$

Moving left requires $v(t)<0$.

For $0\le t<2$, both factors are negative, so $v(t)>0$.
For $2<t<6$, the factors have opposite signs, so $v(t)<0$.
For $t>6$, both factors are positive, so $v(t)>0$.

The particle moves left for $2<t<6$, with $t$ measured in seconds. At the endpoints it is at rest.

coverage.summary: Authored six worked examples covering all distinct assessed methods, using changed values and supplied booklet methods. Questions and solutions remain separate and editable; solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. Aligned calculations use relation gutters without adding phantom equals to independent equations. These algebraic tasks need no diagrams. Existing examples were empty. Assessments were classified only and were neither changed nor re-audited. No files were written; independent review and actual visual capture remain later stages.

examples.derivation: Differentiating x(t) gives v(t)=6t²−10t+4. Initial velocity is x'(0)=4 m/s; v(2)=24−20+4=8 m/s. Both are positive, indicating motion right.
v(t)=3t²−18t+15=3(t−1)(t−5), so rest occurs at 1 s and 5 s. Substitution gives x(1)=1−9+15+4=11 m and x(5)=125−225+75+4=−21 m.
x(t)=(t−3)(t−6), so the origin passages occur at 3 s and 6 s. Differentiation gives v(t)=2t−9; hence v(3)=−3 m/s and v(6)=3 m/s, indicating left then right.

Setting x(t)=5 gives t²−8t+7=(t−1)(t−7)=0. The first admissible time is 1 s. Since v(t)=2t−8, its velocity then is −6 m/s. This nonzero-position adaptation uses the explicitly retained accepted assessment method.
The velocities are v_A(t)=2t+4 and v_B(t)=3t²−4t−5. Equating them gives 3t²−6t−9=3(t−3)(t+1)=0. Only t=3 s satisfies t≥0; both velocities then equal 10 m/s.
v(t)=3t²−24t+36=3(t−2)(t−6). It is positive for 0≤t<2, negative for 2<t<6, and positive for t>6. Thus motion left occurs precisely between 2 s and 6 s, excluding the stationary endpoints.
